forces.title: AI drives unprecedented demand for semiconductors and components
forces.description: The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure, particularly hyperscalers' investments in data centers, is creating a surge in demand for leading-edge chips and high-bandwidth memory (HBM). This unprecedented demand is expected to sustain high growth in the overall semiconductor market, reaching $2.3 trillion by 2030, directly benefiting technology distributors of these critical hardware and components as they meet the needs of a booming AI ecosystem.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Supply-demand imbalance sustains high prices for key components
forces.description: A persistent supply shortage for leading-edge chips (e.g., 3nm, 5nm) and HBM, coupled with surging AI-driven demand, is causing average selling prices (ASPs) to rise significantly. This departure from historical patterns, with 3nm and 5nm wafer ASPs increasing by over 2% annually, provides a favorable pricing environment for technology distributors of these high-value components, boosting revenue potential per unit despite potential volume constraints.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Ongoing supply constraints challenge sourcing of advanced semiconductors
forces.description: The global semiconductor industry faces a persistent supply-demand imbalance, particularly for leading-edge chips and high-bandwidth memory (HBM). This shortage is expected to last for at least three to five more years, making it challenging for technology distributors to consistently source sufficient volumes of these critical components. While high ASPs can mitigate revenue impact, the inability to fulfill all customer orders poses a significant operational challenge and potential for lost sales.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Energy scarcity may slow European data center and AI infrastructure growth
forces.description: McKinsey warns that Europe may lag other regions in data center buildout due to constraints in energy availability and affordability. As AI data centers are highly energy-intensive, any slowdown in their expansion within Europe could translate into reduced demand for the hardware, semiconductors, and components distributed by IN080305. This regional disadvantage could temper the overall growth seen in global markets, impacting local distribution volumes and opportunities.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Agentic commerce creates new software demand for trust infrastructure
forces.description: The rise of invisible and agentic payments is shifting value to a "control layer" of trust, requiring new software capabilities like machine credentials, dynamic consent, risk controls, and transaction protection. Technology distributors have a new opportunity to provide and integrate these specialized software solutions for financial institutions and businesses, potentially generating recurring revenue streams from licensing and managed services in this evolving FinTech landscape, diversifying their product offerings.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Growing competition erodes HBM gross margins for distributors
forces.description: While high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is a major growth driver, McKinsey forecasts that merchant gross margins for HBM could decline from approximately 80% in 2024 to 50% by 2030. This reduction is primarily attributed to increased competition in the accelerator space, indicating that distributors of HBM will face margin pressure despite strong overall demand, requiring strategic adaptation to maintain profitability in this segment.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Asset-heavy industries adopt AI for maintenance, boosting tech distribution
forces.description: Asset-heavy organizations are fundamentally rewiring their maintenance processes with AI and technology to improve efficiency, reliability, and reduce costs. This structural shift creates significant demand for new digital solutions, including gen-AI assisted workflows, agentic AI scheduling tools, and integrated technology platforms. Technology distributors and VARs are positioned to benefit by providing the necessary hardware, software, and critical deployment, support, and managed services to enable this transformation across various industries in Europe.
forces.source_title: Maintenance meets AI: A proven approach for asset-heavy industries

viewpoints.title: Agentic commerce creates new software distribution opportunities in trust infrastructure
viewpoints.description: McKinsey predicts agentic commerce will shift payments value from customer interfaces to an "infrastructure of trust." This creates demand for new software products like machine credentials, consent management, risk controls, and transaction protection. Technology distributors and VARs are well-positioned to capitalize on this by providing these software solutions and bundling deployment, support, and managed services. The B2B segment, especially agentic treasury management, is seen as an early and significant commercial opportunity for such integrated tech solutions, driving new revenue streams for distributors.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: AI-driven maintenance solutions drive demand for integrated enterprise technology
viewpoints.description: McKinsey highlights that asset-heavy industries are undergoing a structural transformation through AI and technology adoption in maintenance. This creates substantial demand for gen-AI workflows, health-monitoring models, and agentic AI scheduling tools. Technology distributors and VARs are crucial in delivering these "digital solutions sourced from different vendors" and integrating them into "AI-driven technology platforms." This shift offers significant opportunities for IN080305 to provide hardware, software, and bundle deployment, support, and managed services for these complex enterprise solutions, transforming maintenance into a value creator.
viewpoints.source_title: Maintenance meets AI: A proven approach for asset-heavy industries

viewpoints.title: AI to sustain high growth and ASPs in semiconductor distribution market
viewpoints.description: McKinsey forecasts unprecedented, sustained growth in the global semiconductor market, projected to reach $2.3 trillion by 2030, largely driven by AI infrastructure investments from hyperscalers. This surge in demand, particularly for leading-edge chips and high-bandwidth memory (HBM), will keep average selling prices (ASPs) high due to persistent supply-demand imbalance. Technology distributors specializing in semiconductors and components are poised to benefit significantly from this market expansion and favorable pricing environment, albeit with the challenge of sourcing constrained supply.
viewpoints.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

demand_drivers.description: Hyperscalers are planning cumulative capital expenditures of $800 billion in 2026 and $1 trillion in 2027, with the vast majority directed toward AI infrastructure, fueling demand for chips and memory components distributed by IN080305.

Chip sales for servers and data centers are the most powerful growth force, expected to rise from $330 billion in 2025 to $1.2 trillion by 2030 at a 29% CAGR, creating significant demand for hardware and components.

pnl_drivers.description: Intensifying supply-demand imbalance, particularly for leading-edge chips and HBM, is pushing ASPs significantly higher. This results in increased revenue per unit for distributed components, positively impacting distributors' top line.

market_sizing.methodology: Base case projection for global semiconductor market value, including fabless, OEMs with in-house design, and captive-chip players. It revises an earlier forecast of $1.6 trillion from Autumn 2025. This market includes products distributed by IN080305.
market_sizing.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

demand_drivers.description: The shift to agentic commerce requires new trust infrastructure products (credentials, mandate/consent management, risk controls, agent wallets, transaction protection) which are software-based and represent new revenue pools for tech distributors and VARs.

Traditional e-procurement and treasury management are evolving towards autonomous agents that source, evaluate bids, negotiate, and execute settlements, creating demand for sophisticated B2B software and underlying IT infrastructure.

new_opportunities.description: Technology distributors can offer new software products related to machine identity, consent management, policy control, and transaction protection for agentic commerce, generating recurring fees and premiums from these evolving FinTech solutions.

Distributors and VARs can provide deployment, support, and managed services for complex AI-driven B2B software, such as autonomous treasury agents and e-procurement systems, tapping into early commercial opportunities and value-added revenue.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Bundled Services for B2B AI Solutions

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of how agentic AI reshapes payment economics by shifting value to an "infrastructure of trust" and creating new product capabilities (e.g., credentials, consent management, risk controls, agent wallets, transaction protection). The B2B segment, including autonomous treasury management and e-procurement agents, is identified as a significant, early-moving opportunity pool for these software and service offerings, driving demand for technology distribution.
